name: Victorian parlour

influenced_by: industrial-era textile manufacturing (patterned wallpaper and fabric became affordable)

places: Britain and its empire; US upper-middle-class homes
reacts_against: the sparer Georgian interiors that preceded it, filling every surface (a reaction, in turn, that 20th-century modernism would itself react against).
revivals: a recurring maximalist-interior reference, most recently inside cluttercore moodboards

wiki_facts.key_motifs: Ornate detailing, Gothic Revival architecture, industrial machinery, gaslight, pocket watches, corsets, top hats, mourning rituals, strict social codes, intricate patterns, dark romanticism, scientific curiosity, domesticity, elaborate hairstyles, crinolines, bustles
wiki_facts.key_colours: Ochre, russet, beige, brown, taupe, black, white, royal blue, crimson, deep jewel tones (emerald green, ruby red, sapphire blue)

findings: mostly muted — about 71% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
